$comment: Gemfall beat 5 on the River Road (docs/campaigns/gemfall.md, 5A). `allies` is set exactly once, by the three choices of scene_who_to_tell, which every path to every ending passes through once (it sits before the crossing and nothing loops back). `cult` is optional and only ever set by scene_cult_pitch, on one of two choices, so no path sets both. The setback needs a failed span crossing, then a failed wolf check or the fight picked, and the fight lost. The expansion's spine episodes (brass south, tremor, Nim's pony, old marks, survey guard, crack string, stones vote, span question, pack crossing, rim lookout) set only chapter-local flags; allies is still set only in scene_who_to_tell.
title: The Broken Bridge

plate.narration: A crack runs through the Northern River Bridge. A griffin engineer crouches beside it with chalk and a clipboard. Beyond the barriers, travelers wait to cross. The stones need a careful look before the road can carry on.

objectives.label: Helped somebody whose rush was over
Plotted the outline of the truth yourselves

goal.text: Cross the cracked bridge, and find out what its cracks are saying.

steps.label: Get down to the bridge foot

facet_clerks.name: The Clerk's Stone
facet_clerks.text: Logged, tagged 4117, and crossing westbound. Then, very irregularly, not.

scene_bridge.narration: Cross the cracked Northern River Bridge and find out what its cracks are saying. Skywardens in silver and violet let a few travelers over at a time. Coming south are prospectors whose rush is over. Nobody is singing. The bridge looks like a plate glued by somebody in a hurry.

choices.label: Join the ration line
Circle the cracked spans first

scene_spans_from_above.narration: From the air the crack is not one crack. It is dozens, and they all lean the same way, like grass in a wind. The wind is coming from the mountain. A warden engineer on the bridge looks up, sees you, and writes something down.

choices.label: Land and join the line

scene_soup_line.narration: A woman named Hollis stirs a bathtub-sized soup pot. DEEP HOLLOW is stitched on her apron. She feeds a muddy prospector before asking anything. His wheelbarrow has lost a wheel. He is holding the soup much more carefully.

choices.label: Take a bowl and listen
Fix the prospector's wheelbarrow
Thank her and keep your place

scene_soup_line_fix_barrow.narration: You knock the wheel back on with a rock. The prospector gives you his luck pebble, the only thing he has left. It is not a gem. He says it worked anyway.

choices.label: Take a bowl and sit down

scene_cult_pitch.narration: Hollis talks while she ladles, gently, like she's telling you the weather. "The world's rules are broken, love. Look at this line. The power under the mountain could write new ones. The seal on it isn't a lock. It's a lid on the cure." She nods at a jar labeled THE BREAK. It is half full of humming stones.

choices.label: Say no, kindly
Drop a coin in the jar
Finish your soup and say nothing

scene_cult_pitch_finish_soup.narration: Hollis refills your bowl without asking. You finish without answering her pitch. The jar hums behind her; you can still hear it at the bridge foot.

choices.label: Walk on to the bridge foot

scene_cult_pitch_drop_stone.narration: You drop a coin into the jar marked THE BREAK, in among the humming stones. The whole jar hums louder for a moment, like a hive woken up. Hollis's eyes shine. She writes your names in a little book with a soft pencil, and gives you a second bowl, and you are not sure how you feel about any of it.

choices.label: Walk on to the bridge foot

scene_cult_pitch_say_no_kindly.narration: "No, thank you," you say, kindly. Hollis does not stop ladling. "That's all right, love," she says. "Soup's still free." She means it, which is the part that stays with you all the way to the bridge.

choices.label: Walk on to the bridge foot

scene_clerk.narration: At the bridge foot, warden clerk Pellam logs every passing gem and keeps none. "Logged is not owned," he says. "Owned is not my department." A carter brings gem 4117. Its hum makes his pen leap off the page.

choices.label: Ask the carter what she'd take for it
Find a rule in Pellam's big book
Let it cross, and write down where it's going
Risk finding the transfer rule before the cart leaves

check_carter.prompt: Talk a tired carter into trading gem 4117

onSuccess.narration: She has been listening to that gem hum for nine days. "Take it," she says. "Give me a song I can sing over it instead." You give her the best one you know.

onFailure.narration: "Promised to a buyer in the foothills," she says, and clicks to her mule. Gem 4117 hums away west across the bridge.

check_ledger.prompt: Find the rule that lets a logged gem change hands

onSuccess.narration: Page four hundred and twelve: a logged gem may be transferred at the crossing if both parties sign and the clerk is not on his lunch. Pellam checks his watch. He is not on his lunch.

onFailure.narration: You find a rule about goats, a rule about very large goats, and a rule about goats that are actually two children in a coat. By the time you look up, gem 4117 is across.

scene_clerk_stone.narration: Pellam crosses out WESTBOUND, writes EASTBOUND, crosses that out, and writes WITH THEM, pointing at you. "Very irregular," he says. "Entirely legal." The stone is cool and heavy, and its hum makes your teeth feel fizzy.

choices.label: Go and see the engineers

scene_engineers.narration: Engineer Brask pins every bridge crack in red on a chalk survey. She has a pencil behind each ear and has forgotten the third in her hair. She frowns at the drawing, as though it has said something rude.

choices.label: Lay your evidence beside the survey
Tell her the cracks all lean one way
Unroll your copy of the old marks
Risk sketching the whole account from memory

check_outline.prompt: Plot everything you've seen since Bramblewood against the cracks

onSuccess.narration: You draw it in chalk: the old note the troll's bridge hums, the bent pride roads, the spiraling sashes. Then you draw the cracks over the top.

onFailure.narration: Your map comes out looking like a cat walked across it. Brask takes the chalk, says "no, no, you're right, look," and draws it again properly.

scene_outline.narration: Everything points the same way. The old note the troll's bridge hums, the pride roads, the sashes, the cracks: all bending around the stones, and all of it older than the mountain's name. The stones did not come from the eruption. They were there first. And the land has been keeping records the whole time. Brask goes very quiet and sits down on a bucket.

choices.label: Sit down with her

rest_tent.narration: The engineers share strong tea. Every cup has a tremor ripple. Outside, the bridge creaks. Rest and decide who should hear what you found.

choices.label: Talk it over

scene_who_to_tell.narration: Tell the wardens here, and they can use the survey to manage the crossing. Send the news with Nim the bell-rider, and the gathering towns will hear it. Or keep it close until you know more. Who should hear the outline first?

choices.label: Tell the wardens, right now
Send it north with Nim the bell-rider
Keep it close, for now

scene_told_wardens.narration: Brask writes everything down and underlines the mountain three times. "This changes the arithmetic." She gives you a crossing pass. She has underlined that too.

choices.label: Out to the bridge

scene_told_gatherers.narration: Nim listens, rings her bell once, and turns Pepper north. "Grandmother is going to say she told everyone." For once, Pepper does not argue.

choices.label: Out to the bridge

scene_kept_close.narration: You fold the survey into your safest pocket. Brask keeps her measurements, but your observations travel with you. Nobody else gets the whole account today.

choices.label: Out to the bridge

scene_crossing.narration: The cracked span sways under the last cart. A warden waits with her flag. Use what you prepared, show a crossing pass if you have one, or take an ordinary ration turn. Below, the river is very loud.

choices.label: Take your ration turn on the span
Show Brask's crossing pass
Keep to the east rail, like the Brassbuckles' map says
Carry everyone over the gap, unofficially
Have a thornguard brace the rail for everyone
Use the rope brace you practiced with the apprentices
Cross in the quiet interval you recorded

check_span.prompt: Cross the swaying span before the warden's flag drops

onSuccess.narration: Step, sway, step, sway, and you're over. The warden at the far end gives you a very small nod, which from a Skywarden is practically a hug.

onFailure.narration: Halfway across, the bridge gives a long groan and the flag slams down. "Span closed! Everybody back!" The only other way over is the old pride ford, underneath.

scene_under_bridge.narration: Under the bridge the stone is warm from the sun, and somebody else has noticed. A pack of cinder wolves lies heaped against the pillars, ember-eyed and cold, a long way from home. They lift their heads at the hum in your packs and do not like it at all.

choices.label: Leave them your supper and tiptoe past
Push through to the ford

check_wolves.prompt: Get the pack interested in supper instead of you

onSuccess.narration: Every nose turns toward the supper. You wade the ford with your boots in your hands while a dozen ember eyes ignore you completely.

onFailure.narration: The supper is gone in four seconds. The pack looks at you as if to say: is that all?

encounter_wolves.narration: The pack spreads along both shallow crossings, guarding the warm side of the river.

onVictory.narration: The wolves give way, grumbling, and pile back up against their warm pillar. You wade across while they pretend they meant to move anyway.

onDefeat.narration: The pack holds the ford, and you end up back on the south bank, soggy and outnumbered.

scene_griffin_shortcut.narration: One at a time, you carry everybody over the broken gap, wings beating hard over the cold water. Behind you, clerk Pellam watches the whole thing, sighs, and writes UNRATIFIED in his ledger in very large letters.

choices.label: On to the far rim

scene_far_rim.narration: Beyond the bridge, grass gives way to red stones. The foothills of Mount Red Sky glow ahead. You climb toward their rim with the outline of the truth in your packs.

choices.label: Climb to the rim

rest_end.narration: You camp on the rim and look down. The foothills are full of tiny campfires, thousands of them, all the rush in the world. Above it all, the mountain glows. The stones hum. Somebody has to put this all together on one table, and tomorrow, at Redspire, the wardens' citadel, somebody will.

variants.text: Your work at the crack became a way across the bridge.

rest_setback.narration: Nobody is hurt. The wolves just wanted the warm side more. You wait two whole days on the south bank for the span to open again, while the rush gets further ahead and the mountain glows a little brighter every night. In the end Pellam waves you across himself. "Logged," he says. "Late. But logged."

variants.text: Your work at the crack became a way across the bridge.

scene_brass_south.narration: Six tired people in dented brass hats push an empty wheelbarrow south. The Brassbuckle Expedition. They stop when they see you. Nobody smiles smoothly this time.

choices.label: Ask them what happened up north
Share your supper with them
Ask them the troll's question

scene_brass_south_ask_what.narration: "Full," says the tallest Brassbuckle. "The foothills are full. Every stone has three people standing on it already, and a warden writing it down." He looks at the empty barrow. "We should have told the troll a story," he says. "We'd have been first, then. Probably." Nobody believes him, including him.

choices.label: Wish them a good road home

scene_brass_south_share_supper.narration: You share your supper with all six of them, sitting on the empty barrow. They eat like people who have not eaten since the foothills. Afterwards the smallest Brassbuckle gives you a folded paper. "Our map of the span," she says. "Keep to the east rail. It sways least. We were going to sell it."

choices.label: Wave them off south

scene_brass_south_ask_question.narration: "Where did you get that?" you ask, nodding at the barrow. "And where is it going?" The Brassbuckles look into it. There is nothing in it at all. "Nowhere, now," says the tallest at last. "Home." He sounds, for the first time since Stone Crossing, like he means it.

choices.label: Wish them a good road home

scene_tremor.narration: The ground gives a long shudder. The ration line wobbles. On a cart beside you, a stack of crates leans. The tired carter reaches for it too late.

choices.label: Catch the crates
Look at what the shudder did to the road

check_crates.prompt: Everybody grab at the toppling crates

onSuccess.narration: You catch the top crate, then the next, then the next, and stand there holding a wobbling tower until the carter props it back. "Nine days those have been humming at me," she says, wiping her face. "Nine days. Thank you." One crate has a tag on it: 4117.

onFailure.narration: The crates topple straight past your hands and land, thump, thump, thump, in a hay cart. Nothing breaks. One of them bursts open, and it is full of socks. "Not that one," says the tired carter. "The humming ones are underneath." One tag says 4117.

scene_tremor_look_down.narration: When the shudder stops, the road at your feet is crazed with cracks as thin as hairs. Dozens of them. And every one leans the same way, like grass in a wind, and the wind is coming from the mountain. You look up at the cracked bridge. Its cracks lean the same way too.

choices.label: Shuffle on up the line

scene_nim_pony.narration: Nim, a dragonling bell-rider, argues with her pony Pepper at the bridge foot. She wants north. Pepper wants grass. Her bell keeps ringing while she explains the difference.

choices.label: Cover Pepper's ears and lead her past
Talk to Pepper, slow and quiet
Greet Nim the gathering-town way

scene_nim_pony_hold_pony.narration: You put your hands gently over Pepper's ears and lead her past the humming carts, one slow step at a time. Pepper allows this, as long as you also scratch her nose. "Grandmother says the ponies always know first," Nim tells you. "Grandmother says a lot of things. She is usually right. It's very annoying."

choices.label: Walk on with Nim to the bridge foot

check_pony.narration: Pepper has gone stiff-legged in the road, ears flat, staring at the humming carts. Nim has run out of bell. "She'll stand there till Tuesday," she says. "Do something nice at her."

interaction.cue: Do something calm and kind until Pepper's ears come forward.

options.label: Hum a slow tune
options.reaction: Pepper's ears swivel toward the sound.

options.label: Stroke her nose
options.reaction: Pepper leans into your palm with a sigh.

options.label: Offer a windfall apple
options.reaction: Pepper crunches it and forgets all about the carts.

stages: She sighs, and her feet unfreeze.

onSuccess.narration: Pepper sighs, and walks on past the carts as if it had been her idea all along. Nim stares at you. "Grandmother can do that," she says. "Nobody else can do that." She presses three coins into your hand. "Bell-rider's tip. Do not tell Grandmother."

onFailure.narration: Pepper sighs, and walks on past the carts as if it had been her idea all along. Nim stares at you. "Grandmother can do that," she says. "Nobody else can do that." She presses three coins into your hand. "Bell-rider's tip. Do not tell Grandmother."

scene_nim_pony_bell_greeting.narration: You bow and ring an imaginary bell three times, high, low, high, the way they do in the gathering towns. Nim squeaks. "You're from the towns!" Even Pepper looks impressed. Nim walks with you all the way to the bridge foot, telling you which grandmothers are feuding this year. It is most of them.

choices.label: Walk on with Nim to the bridge foot

scene_old_marks.narration: Down at the bridge foot, where the river has scrubbed the oldest stones bare, there are marks. Carved lines, worn almost smooth, under the bridge's own stones, as if the bridge had been built on top of somebody else's writing. "Always been there," says a passing warden. "Nobody reads them."

choices.label: Make a charcoal rubbing of the marks
Lay a palm on the stone, like Old Lintel
Look at the marks the way your people read paths

check_rubbing.narration: The marks are worn so smooth that charcoal only catches them when the light is just right. The warden lifts her lantern, and the carved shapes glow, one at a time. "Quick," she says. "Light moves." Watch them go by, then draw them back in the same order.

interaction.cue: Watch the marks glow, then draw them back in order.

onSuccess.narration: Paper, charcoal, rub, rub, rub. The lines come up black and clear: a spiral, curling around and around a little circle in the middle. Just like the sashes at the waystation. Just like the pride roads. You roll the paper up very carefully.

onFailure.narration: Paper, charcoal, rub. What comes out is a perfect picture of a warden's boot, because a warden was standing on the corner of your paper. She asks if she can keep it. You let her.

onAssisted.narration: The warden holds her lantern still for as long as you need. Paper, charcoal, rub, rub, rub. The lines come up black and clear: a spiral, curling around and around a little circle in the middle. Just like the sashes at the waystation. You roll the paper up very carefully.

scene_old_marks_palm.narration: You lay a palm flat on the old stone, the way Old Lintel does. For a long moment, nothing. Then, deep down, so low you feel it more than hear it: the note. The same note your packs hum. The stone under the bridge was humming it long before there was any bridge, or any rush.

choices.label: Go up to the clerk's table

scene_old_marks_read_marks.narration: You notice what everybody walks past. These marks are not just old. They have been carved again, and again, over hundreds of years, the old cuts deepened, the spiral kept clear. Somebody, or something, has been keeping this record for a very long time. You copy every line.

choices.label: Go up to the clerk's table

scene_survey_guard.narration: Outside the engineers' tent stands Corporal Tibbet, who is very new, very junior, and very serious. His helmet is too big. "No entry," he says, "without a pass. Or a reason. A good reason. In writing." He holds out a clipboard. It already has a pencil on a string.

choices.label: Tell him why you need to see the survey
Write your reason down, as asked
Show him the stone Pellam logged to you

check_tibbet.prompt: Convince a very serious corporal to let you in

onSuccess.narration: You tell him about the old note the troll's bridge hums, and the bent roads, and the spiraling sashes. Tibbet listens with his mouth slightly open. Then he remembers he is a corporal, closes it, salutes, and lifts the tent flap for you.

onFailure.narration: Tibbet listens to every word, writes "REASON: LONG" on his clipboard, and says no. Then an engineer pokes her head out, says "Tibbet, let them hold the string," and pulls you around the side of the tent.

scene_survey_guard_write_it.narration: You write your reason on his clipboard, in your best letters: WE THINK THE STONES ARE OLDER THAN THE MOUNTAIN. Tibbet reads it. He reads it again. He goes slightly pale under the big helmet, and holds the tent flap open for you without another word.

choices.label: Go on around the tent

scene_survey_guard_clerks_stone.narration: You show Tibbet the Clerk's Stone, tag 4117, with WITH THEM written in Pellam's hand. Tibbet reads the tag, stands up very straight, and salutes the stone. Then, because he is not sure, he salutes you too. "Logged goods may pass," he says, and opens the flap.

choices.label: Go on around the tent

scene_crack_string.narration: Two apprentices measure a crack with knotted string. Help tension the line and learn to brace a crossing rope, or study the chalk marks to learn when the span settles between carts. There is time for one job before the tent meeting. An apprentice has chalk on both eyebrows.

choices.label: Hold the string perfectly still
Read the ladder of chalk marks

check_string.narration: Behind the tent, the apprentice is stretching a knotted string along the crack. "Hold this end?" she asks. "It only reads true when it's tight. One hand reads the knots, everyone else pulls."

interaction.cue: Friends pull the string tight while someone reads the knots.

onSuccess.narration: You hold it steady as a heron's leg. The apprentice counts the knots, then counts again. "A hair wider than yesterday," she says, and chalks it. "It's always a hair wider than yesterday." She says it as if she is getting tired of hair.

onFailure.narration: A breeze catches the string and it wiggles like a worm. You try again. It wiggles more. The apprentice laughs, measures it herself in a moment, and chalks the mark. "A hair wider than yesterday," she says. "Always is."

onAssisted.narration: The apprentice props one end while you tension the line. With her help, you learn how to brace the crossing rope.

scene_crack_string_read_chalk.narration: The chalk marks show each widening crack. Beside them are cart counts and checks made while the span rests. An apprentice shows you the safe interval after the last cart leaves. You copy it for the crossing. Her eyebrows shed a little chalk onto the page.

choices.label: Go into the engineers' tent

scene_engineers_rubbing.narration: You unroll the copy of the old marks from under the bridge and lay it beside the survey. Brask looks from one to the other, and back again. The spiral on the old stone and the cracks in her new drawing curl around the very same point. She takes the pencil from behind her left ear, and then the right.

choices.label: Let her see the whole thing

choice_stones_on_table.narration: Brask looks up from her bucket at your packs. "Those are humming," she says. "Everything you've carried. May I see them? On the survey?" The whole tent goes quiet to hear what you'll say. Will you lay your stones on the table? Everybody vote.

choices.label: Lay every stone on the survey
Keep the packs shut
Show her the Pride Stone that no pride would touch

choice_stones_on_table_lay_out.narration: You set your stones out on the big chalk drawing, one by one. They hum together, a little chord. Brask's tea starts to ripple in its cup. Without seeming to notice, she moves the cup to the far end of the table, then a bit further, then puts it on the floor.

choices.label: Sit down with the engineers

choice_stones_on_table_keep_shut.narration: "Not yet," you say, and keep your packs shut. Brask nods slowly. "Fair," she says. "You carried them." She writes KEPT SHUT in the corner of the survey, very neatly, and underlines it, which makes you feel both proud and a little bit watched.

choices.label: Sit down with the engineers

choice_stones_on_table_pride_stone.narration: You set the Pride Stone on the table and tell her where it came from: the middle of the widest bend, where no pride would set a paw. Brask writes PRIDE COUNTRY: AVOIDED BY EVERYONE on her survey and draws a circle around it. Then she draws a second circle around that one.

choices.label: Sit down with the engineers

scene_span_question.narration: At the bridge end, the warden with the flag stops you. She looks at your packs, and then at you, and asks, very seriously, "Where did you get that? And where is it going?" It is Old Lintel's question, word for word, a whole country away from his bridge.

choices.label: Answer her honestly
Ask where she heard that question
Tell her the river asked you first

scene_span_question_answer.narration: You tell her all of it, from the Exchange gutter to the bridge foot, as honestly as you can. She writes it down. At the end she looks at what she has written for quite a while. "Nobody else has answered properly," she says. "They just say 'mine' and 'north.'"

choices.label: Wait for your turn

scene_span_question_ask_back.narration: "From a carter," she says, "who had it from a centaur, who had it from a manticore, who had it from a troll, apparently." She shrugs. "It's a good question. Everybody's asking it now. Nobody has a good answer." She waves her flag at the next cart and asks them too.

choices.label: Wait for your turn

scene_span_question_river_asked.narration: "The river asked us first," you say. "It took us all the way to the sea to ask it." The warden blinks. Then she laughs, a real laugh, the first one you have heard from a Skywarden. "Well," she says, "did you have an answer for it?" You are still working on that.

choices.label: Wait for your turn

scene_pack_crossing.narration: Pellam offers the wardens' logged gem cart or your own arms for the packs. "Logged is not owned." He licks his pencil. The cart hums like a hive; its mule looks unimpressed.

choices.label: Carry them across in your own arms
Send them over on the gem cart
Wrap them in Ossley's reed knot first

scene_pack_crossing_carry.narration: Pellam writes CARRIED, BY HAND, BY CHOICE. You keep the packs close. He considers adding an underline, then saves it for later.

choices.label: Step up to the span

scene_pack_crossing_cart.narration: Your packs ride on the gem cart. The bridge groans; every warden checks the span. On the far approach, Pellam hands the packs back, still logged, still yours.

choices.label: Step up to the span

scene_pack_crossing_reed_knot.narration: You wind Old Ossley's wet reed knot around your packs, and the hum goes soft, like a river a long way off. Pellam leans close and listens. He writes HUMMING GOODS, and crosses it out, and writes QUIETER THAN EXPECTED. "Most irregular," he says, and sounds pleased.

choices.label: Step up to the span

check_span_quiet.prompt: Cross along the steady east rail before the flag drops

onSuccess.narration: Along the east rail the span hardly sways at all. You walk over almost easily, and the warden at the far end gives you a very small nod. The Brassbuckles' map was right. You hope somebody tells them.

onFailure.narration: The east rail is steadier, but not steady enough. Halfway over, the bridge groans and the flag slams down. "Span closed! Everybody back!" The only other way over is the old pride ford, underneath.

scene_rim_lookout.narration: A fresh centaur marker reads REDSPIRE, ONE DAY. Bracken Swiftmile skids up behind you, sash full of letters. "Relay waits for nobody. But it does catch up. Anything going south?"

choices.label: Send word south to the pride and the troll
Pay Bracken a coin to carry your letters first
Try to count the campfires
Fly up and look for Redspire
Have a duskrunner dart ahead and count the fires

scene_rim_lookout_send_word.narration: You write two short letters. One for Elder Sefa: the cubs were right, the stones really are singing. One for Old Lintel: we are finding out. Bracken tucks them in her sash. "Troll'll take a year to read it," she says. "He'll hear every word, though." Then she is gone, south, at a gallop.

choices.label: Make camp on the rim

check_fires.prompt: Count the rush's campfires in the foothills below

onSuccess.narration: You count in hundreds, then in patches, then in valleys. Bracken helps. Your best guess is four thousand and twelve, and Bracken writes it down to carry south. "Biggest rush in living memory," she says, and whistles. "And all of it humming."

onFailure.narration: One, two, three... you lose count at three hundred and something, when a cloud moves and a whole valley of fires appears at once. "More than stars," says Bracken, and that will have to do. She trots off south with your news.

scene_rim_lookout_fly_redspire.narration: You climb high into the red evening. Far off, on the highest peak of the foothills, stands a tall black citadel, shining like a wet stone: Redspire, where the wardens keep their records. Every road in the foothills seems to lead to it. You glide back down and tell Bracken. She already knew, but she lets you tell her anyway.

choices.label: Make camp on the rim

interaction_bowls.narration: You help the soup woman serve the tired travelers. The carter takes off her hat, considers using it as a bowl, and accepts a proper bowl instead. Nobody has to race for supper. Not a drop spills. The last bowl reaches the tired carter, who drinks it with both hands. "Humming gives me the shakes," she says. The woman with the ladle nods at you, as if you had passed a test she never said she was giving, and tucks a wrapped supper into your pack.

choices.label: Continue together

interaction_level.narration: Brask brings a tray of water with a tiny cork boat. "Engineers' level." Carry it flat across the approach planks. The boat must stay in the middle. It has no interest in going overboard.

interaction.cue: Everyone lift or lower your side until the water is flat, then carry the tray.

onSuccess.narration: The cork boat never moves. "Level to a hair," says Brask, and writes it down with the pencil she had forgotten about. "The approach is sound. It is the middle that worries me."

onFailure.narration: The water slops over the side and the cork boat goes for a swim. "Either the plank leans or you do," says Brask, mopping the tray with her hat. "Probably both."

onAssisted.narration: Brask steadies one side of the tray herself, and the water lies flat. "Level to a hair," she says. "The approach is sound. It is the middle that worries me."

scene_lantern_wisps.narration: The bridge lanterns are lit for the evening ration, and two wisps have noticed. They are tiny, pale and giggling, and they have untied the lantern strings on the gem cart to see what happens. The cart's lamps swing wild. A mule starts to complain. "Get them off the cart before the whole line spooks!" shouts Brask.

choices.label: Shoo the wisps off the cart

encounter_wisps.narration: The wisps zip around the cart, tugging lantern strings and giggling. Drive them off before the mule bolts.

scene_wisps_shooed.narration: The wisps squeak, wobble and bob away over the river, still giggling. The mule stops complaining. Brask catches a spoonful of their leftover glow in an empty jar and screws on the lid. "Free light," she says. "Take it. The tent has plenty."

choices.label: Step up to the span

scene_wisps_scattered.narration: The wisps swirl until the whole bridge is dizzy sparkles. Brask bangs a pot lid against the cart rail, loud and honest, and the wisps pop away over the river like soap bubbles. She wraps everybody in blankets and hands out hot tea. Nobody gets a jar of glow tonight, but the mule is calm again.

choices.label: Step up to the span

scene_rim_lookout_pay.narration: You press a coin into Bracken's hand, and she tucks your letters in the front of her sash, ahead of everyone else's. "Priority post," she says. "First in the bag, first out." She is gone, south, at a gallop, and one very old letter flutters out behind her and lands on your boot.

choices.label: Make camp on the rim

interaction_crossing_signal.narration: Before your turn, the warden shows the bridge signals: wait, walk, wait. The river drowns out shouted instructions. Repeat the flags in order so you can follow them when you are on the span.

interaction.cue: Watch the signals, then repeat them in order.

interaction_flag_rope.narration: The warden catches her loose signal rope and ties it where the next watcher can reach it. She brings you beside the rail. Now there is time to learn what her flags mean.

choices.label: Continue together

interaction_transfer_rule.narration: Pellam opens the transfer page. The carter agrees to give you the humming gem in return for a song she can sing over it. Put the steps in order before she signs. Pellam has a fresh pen. He is keeping it firmly on the page.

interaction.cue: Share the rule clues and prepare the agreed transfer.
clues: Match the gem tag before anyone signs.
The carter and the new carriers both sign after the tag is checked.
Record the new destination after both signatures.

onSuccess.narration: Tag checked, both signatures made, new destination recorded. You sing for the carter. Pellam approves the transfer.

onFailure.narration: You find a rule about goats, a rule about very large goats, and a rule about goats that are actually two children in a coat. By the time you look up, gem 4117 is across.

onAssisted.narration: Pellam points to each step while you check it. The carter signs, you sing, and the agreed transfer is recorded with help.

interaction_survey_evidence.narration: Put what you noticed beside the crack survey. Say one observation aloud, or ask Brask to read one of her measurements. Each hero adds a piece. Brask moves her tea before the chalk arrives. Experience has taught her this.

choices.label: Describe a road we walked
Describe what we noticed near stones
Ask Brask for a bridge measurement

interaction_survey_line.narration: The warden has checked the crossing rope. Use the tension you practiced: hold it while the acting hero guides the passage. Alone, use its fixed support. The chalk on the rope must stay beside the chalk on the post.

interaction.cue: Brace the checked rope while the acting hero guides the crossing.

onSuccess.narration: The brace holds steady. The warden guides you across the checked span.

onFailure.narration: The rope slackens. The warden closes the span and leads you down to the old ford.

onAssisted.narration: The warden braces the post beside you. Together you keep the rope taut and cross.

interaction_settled_span.narration: The last cart clears the span. Your copied measurements show the quiet interval, and the warden confirms it with her flag. Wait for the gold signal before stepping onto the checked section.

interaction.cue: Step when the gold signal marks the settled interval.

onSuccess.narration: You use the recorded interval. The warden keeps the carts waiting until you are across.

onFailure.narration: You stop when the flag drops. The span needs another inspection; the warden sends you to the old ford.

onAssisted.narration: The warden calls the quiet interval from your notes. With her help, you cross before the carts move.

interaction_survey_evidence_response_roa.narration: Your road goes beside the crack lines. Brask checks where it bends. Your observations and the engineers' measurements fit on one survey. Together you compare the bends.

choices.label: Continue together

interaction_survey_evidence_response_sto.narration: Brask marks the places you describe, asking where the observation came from. Your observations and the engineers' measurements fit on one survey. Together you compare the bends.

choices.label: Continue together

interaction_survey_evidence_response_mea.narration: Brask reads yesterday and today from the survey. One pencil falls out of her hair. Your observations and the engineers' measurements fit on one survey. Together you compare the bends.

choices.label: Continue together

voiceGuide.tone: busy, gray-coated, a bit solemn, with warm people in it; the moment the party sees the whole shape of the clue
forbidden: the cult as villains; they are kind first, always
naming what the titan or the Hollow Gate is

npcVoices.hollis: a Deep Hollow Cult recruiter with a giant soup pot; gentle, patient, calls everyone 'love'; feeds people before she says anything; sincerely believes the seal is a lid on a cure
npcVoices.pellam: a Skywarden clerk; dry, precise, logs everything and keeps nothing; 'logged is not owned'; secretly enjoys irregular-but-legal
npcVoices.brask: Skywarden engineer; pencils behind both ears; blunt and honest; talks about arithmetic and acceptable losses but is not unkind
npcVoices.carter: a tired caravan driver; has heard gem 4117 hum for nine days; trades for a song; grateful when you catch her crates
npcVoices.nim: a dragonling bell-rider on a tiny fast pony called Pepper; quick, proud, a little cheeky about her grandmother
npcVoices.brassbuckles: the Brassbuckle Expedition, coming home south with an empty wheelbarrow and dented hats; tired, honest for once
npcVoices.tibbet: Corporal Tibbet, a very new Skywarden guarding the engineers' tent; helmet too big; wants reasons in writing
npcVoices.apprentice: an apprentice engineer measuring the crack with knotted string every evening; 'a hair wider than yesterday'
npcVoices.flag_warden: the Skywarden with the flag at the span; asks the troll's question of every cart
npcVoices.bracken_swiftmile: a relay-running centaur stuffed with letters; quick, cheerful; 'relay waits for nobody, but it does catch up'

interaction_bowls.narration: Hot soup bowls come down the shaky line. Pass them hand to hand to the tired travelers. The carter takes off her hat, considers using it as a bowl, and thinks better of it.

interaction.cue: Catch the bowl, then pass it down the line.

onSuccess.narration: Not a drop spills. The last bowl reaches the tired carter, who drinks it with both hands. "Humming gives me the shakes," she says. The woman with the ladle nods at you, as if you had passed a test she never said she was giving, and tucks a wrapped supper into your pack.

onFailure.narration: One bowl slips, and a prospector catches it on his hat. "Hot hat," he says, bravely. The line laughs, and the soup goes on.

onAssisted.narration: Together you and the carter pass the bowls in a slow, steady row. Not a drop spills, and the woman with the ladle tucks a wrapped supper into your pack.

interaction_flag_rope.narration: The warden gives the signal rope a tug. Its loose end swings out over the bridge rail. Catch it as it swings back, so the flags can keep guiding the carts across.

interaction.cue: Catch the rope when it swings back to the rail.

interaction_survey_evidence.narration: Put what you noticed beside the crack survey. Say one observation aloud, or ask Brask to read one of her measurements. Each hero adds a piece. Brask moves her tea before the chalk arrives. Experience has taught her this.

interaction.cue: Each hero contributes an observation or checks a measurement.
